# Stop the agent before it writes (offline) - generated by build_tapes.py from clips.py; do not edit by hand
# SA lines only: render with digital-demand-factory/screen-demos/generate_two_voice.py

[intro]
SA: "Coding assistants write more of our code every month. A boundary only holds if a machine can check it at the moment a change is proposed. This clip shows the rule, the hook, and a blocked write."

[screen_01]
SA: "The rule lives in archguard dot toml. Each layer lists what it may import. The domain may import itself and a short list from the standard library. Everything else is denied by default."
SA: "The Kiro hook file registers the checker on the PreToolUse event for file writes, so it runs before an agent's edit is applied."

[screen_02]
SA: "The tempting shortcut: add boto3 to the User entity so it can write an audit record. The script replays the exact str replace payload that Kiro sends. The checker reports rule AG001, names the file and line, and explains the fix: define a port in application, implement it in infrastructure, and inject it from the composition root."
SA: "Exit code two means blocked. The replay compares the domain file before and after the attempted write. The agent gets a design task instead of a silent violation."

[screen_03]
SA: "An agent hook only sees agent tool calls. A person can still edit the file directly, so the same checker runs as a git pre-commit hook. This run uses a throwaway clone, stages a boto3 import in the Order entity, and the commit is refused. The real working tree is untouched."

[outro]
SA: "Here is what this does not prove. An agent hook does not see shell commands, and a pre-commit hook can be skipped. For merge enforcement, install the CI workflow from the kit and make it a required check. And a hook does not make an edit correct; tests and review still do that."
SA: "The takeaway: write the boundary down as a file, and check every agent write and every commit against it."
